questions: With kp 3.5 and kd 0.5 on this geometry, does the score return to about 215?
Is oval steering_oscillation below about 0.30, and does the held-back track show line loss beyond 1 per run?
feedback_request.requested_changes_if_any: If the Integrator must change the controller, use kp 3.5 with kd 0.5 (the 215 baseline). Do not change the geometry in this final iteration.

intent: Deliver the proven 215-scoring geometry unchanged for the final unseen-track race. Keep wheel_track 0.09 m, the five 12 mm sensors at x = -0.024 to +0.024 m and y = 0.04 m, wheel radius 0.03 m, body 0.12 x 0.18 m, and mass 0.6 kg. Expected result: a finished or near-finished run on the held-back track, with line loss near 1 per run on the slalom and s-bend and a score close to the 215 development baseline.
learning: Iteration 10 showed that kp 3.2 at kd 0.5 lowered the score from 215 to 175 on unchanged geometry. Yaw gain at kp 3.5 is the better setting on this platform, and the geometry is final.
rationale: This is the final iteration, so this design races the held-back final track and nothing after it can correct it. The best-supported platform is the wheel_track 0.09 m, five-sensor, 12 mm, y = 0.04 m, 0.6 kg geometry from iterations 8 and 9, which scored 215.38 both times. Iteration 10 kept that geometry and changed only the controller to kp 3.2 with kd 0.5. It scored 174.96, and oval steering_oscillation stayed at 0.294, so kp 3.2 is the wrong direction and the cost falls on the controller, not the geometry. Every sensing change (iterations 1 to 3) lowered the score, and narrowing the track to 0.08 m adds about 12 percent more yaw gain per command, which the oscillation already shows is at its limit. A geometry gamble on the last race has no later iteration to recover from, so I hold the proven values unchanged. Expected result: a score near 215 on the development tracks with the Integrator's controller. The Integrator should return to kp 3.5 with kd 0.5, which scored 215.38 on this geometry, rather than kp 3.2.
